sections.heading: FireHydrant buyer question and thesis
sections.body:
incident management; change and problem management; infrastructure monitoring; CI/CD and automation. Free · free · incident management | Pro | Enterprise. Slack, Microsoft Teams, Pagerduty. Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path; Buyers comparing FireHydrant Pro list price to Rootly list price and incident.io Team list price; Orgs that will keep PagerDuty for paging and add FireHydrant for command. FireHydrant is an incident-response and command platform (declare, coordinate, retrospective) with responder-priced packaging. Free covers up to 10 responders. Pro is list price/re. That catalogue mix is the FireHydrant implementation filter — not a generic it-development lecture.

Buyer question: for incident management teams, is FireHydrant worth the Pro unlock, or does Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award kill the rollout?

ROI gate: FireHydrant is worth the Pro spend if incident management + change and problem management are weekly; not worth buying when Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award.

Best for: Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path; Buyers comparing FireHydrant Pro list price to Rootly list price and incident.io Team list price; Orgs that will keep PagerDuty for paging and add FireHydrant for command (Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path).

Poor fit when: Orgs whose primary job is PagerDuty-style on-call paging at enterprise scale; Honeycomb/Datadog observability purchases; ITSM ticket desks without incident command. Avoid if Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award would block go-live.

sections.heading: FireHydrant limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award; On-call paging is not the primary SKU — often paired with PagerDuty; Not observability telemetry (Datadog / Honeycomb) because it forces process changes or add-ons around FireHydrant when incident management is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Free until incident management is mandatory; plan jumps to Pro only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain incident management at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Free · free · incident management | Pro | Enterprise.

Alternative context: unlike PagerDuty, FireHydrant is preferable when Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path because incident management plus incident management match; prefer PagerDuty when Orgs whose primary job is PagerDuty-style on-call paging at enterprise scale because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for FireHydrant
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: FireHydrant is faster for incident management when incident management; change and problem management; infrastructure monitoring; CI/CD and automation is in-product; skip when Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming incident management ownership and Slack before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Integrations in research: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Pagerduty.

Conclusion: FireHydrant is worth it if Teams that want incident command with a 10-responder free path and incident management are weekly; skip FireHydrant if Orgs whose primary job is PagerDuty-style on-call paging at enterprise scale. That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
